claims.text: Oxidation resistance in multiprincipal-element alloys is governed by the formation of a stable, adherent oxide layer.
Material integrity in harsh high-temperature environments is governed by the formation of a stable, adherent oxide layer.
Al can enhance the formation or stability of a protective oxide layer.
Cr can enhance the formation or stability of a protective oxide layer.
A stable oxide layer protects the underlying alloy from further oxidation.
A stable oxide layer protects the underlying alloy from degradation.
Multiprincipal-element alloys containing stabilizing elements such as Al or Cr will have better oxidation resistance than baseline alloys lacking those elements.
Multiprincipal-element alloys containing stabilizing elements such as Al or Cr will retain material integrity better than baseline alloys lacking those elements.
The proposed governing behavior should apply from 800°C to 1200°C.
The proposed governing behavior should apply in oxidizing atmospheres such as air or oxygen.
The specific roles and interactions of different oxide-stabilizing elements are not well understood.
The hypothesis is falsified if alloys containing the proposed stabilizing elements show no improvement in either oxidation resistance or material integrity relative to the baseline.
